title: Settings certifies any string as a working OpenRouter key ('OpenRouter key configured - research bills to it'), and when hosted research then 401s nothing in the trace or stream says so - the local lane fabricated a brief with invented sources
repro: Settings -> AI Providers -> OpenRouter -> Add key -> paste 'sk-or-v1-R15CANARY-this-is-not-a-real-key' -> Save: POST /llm/keys/validate -> {ok:true} (0.24 s), row reads 'Key configured', Tier B card reads 'OpenRouter key configured - research bills to it.' (10-settings-panel-replay.json S2). Then research on Tier B with that key while chat runs on Ollama (vy.py invoke copilot ... --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b --tier tier_b, X-Vysted-Openrouter-Key=<fake>): the stream carries two research_step frames, both status 'ok' ('research:begin', 'research-model:perplexity/sonar - hosted research model'), then 'done' - no error step, no error frame. The 401 message exists only inside the tool result handed to the model; llama3.1:8b answered 'Reliance ... market capitalization of over $200 billion USD' with 'Brief sources: Wikipedia, Forbes, Bloomberg' (none fetched).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-panel-replay.json (S2), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/G01-tierb-fake-openrouter-key.jsonl + .stdout.txt, docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/http-log.jsonl B01-validate-fake-openrouter/B12, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:842-849 (validate = models.list()), sidecar/services/llm/openrouter_catalog.py:15 ('/api/v1/models (no auth, full catalog)'), sidecar/services/agent_tools/deep_research.py:682,723-724 (HTTP error returns ok:false without a _step), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1103-1105
notes: Root cause of the validation half is already COD-llm-adapters-2-4 (code); this is the live user-visible chain it produces on the Tier B surface. Principle: a failure must surface where the user is looking - the only honest copy of '401 - check your OpenRouter key' goes to the model, the trace says ok, and Settings keeps asserting the key bills. Consequence: a mistyped key yields fabricated research (a local model) or a narrated apology at best, with Settings contradicting it. Smallest fix: validate OpenRouter against an authenticated endpoint (GET /api/v1/auth/key or /models/user with the key, 401 -> invalid); in run_research_model_brief emit _step('error', <human message>) before returning ok:false so the trace and brief panel show the failure regardless of the model.

title: Settings key dialog never trims the pasted key: a trailing space or newline turns into 'transport error: Connection error.' (reads as a network outage) for OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq and DeepSeek - onboarding trims, Settings does not
repro: Settings -> AI Providers -> OpenAI -> Add key -> paste a key followed by a space (copy from a password manager / email) -> Save: dialog shows 'transport error: Connection error.' (10-settings-panel-replay.json S3). Same body direct: POST /llm/keys/validate {provider:'openai'|'anthropic'|'groq'|'deepseek', api_key:'<key> '} -> ok:false 'transport error: Connection error.' (B10, B11); with a trailing '\n' -> same for openai/openrouter (B08, B09). Gemini + space -> 'transport error: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. {...}' raw dict. The identical key without the whitespace reaches the provider (B01).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-panel-replay.json (S3), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/http-log.jsonl B08-B11, src/components/KeyEntryDialog.tsx:73,79,181 (raw `key` validated and stored), src/components/OnboardingFlow.tsx:344-354 (onboarding uses key.trim()), sidecar/routers/llm.py:99-111 (no strip; transport exception text returned verbatim)
notes: Principle: normalise at the boundary, and name the real cause. The whitespace makes the Authorization header illegal, so the SDK fails before any request and the router labels it a transport error - the user retries, checks their network, or assumes the provider is down. Two entry points for the same secret disagree (onboarding trims, Settings does not); a whitespace key that ever passes (OpenRouter's public /models) is stored untrimmed in the keychain. Smallest fix: key.trim() in KeyEntryDialog.handleSave (validate + setSecret) and api_key.strip() in LLMKeyValidationRequest.

title: Settings Export carries 3 preference fields and not the research tier, research models, SearXNG URL, default provider/model or module toggles; Import says 'Imported settings.' for any JSON, including {} and another app's file
repro: Set Research tier = Hosted, Deep model = openai/o4-mini-deep-research, custom SearXNG URL, Default provider = OpenAI -> buildSettingsExport() (what 'Export settings' writes) = {version:1, keybindingOverrides:{}, settings:{defaultAgentId:'copilot', region:'IN', deepResearchBackend:'native'}} - none of the four visible choices is in it (S5). The panel copy promises 'your keybinding remaps and preferences (default agent, region, research engine)'; the only research field exported, deepResearchBackend, has no control anywhere in Settings. Import: a file containing '{}' or {theme:'dark',fontSize:14} -> status line 'Imported settings. Secrets re-enter via the keychain.' in green, stores unchanged (S4 empty-object / other-app-json).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-panel-replay.json (S4, S5), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1767-1773 (bundle = keybindings + settings.toBundle only), :1798-1812 (success set unconditionally after two optional ifs), :1847-1850 (copy), src/store/settings.ts:81-85,185-192 (bundle = defaultAgentId/region/deepResearchBackend), `grep -rn setDeepResearchBackend src` -> no UI caller; merged (agent P): docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-plugins-replay.json S2-keybindings-export-import.imports (empty-object, package-json, region-bogus, garbage-bindings all report 'Imported settings.'; a bundle with keybindingOverrides {'no.such.action':'mod+q','palette.open':42} is applied as {'no.such.action':'mod+q'} and wipes the existing remap), src/store/settings.ts:162-176 (setAll merges over seed(), so an imported settings block without a valid region/deepResearchBackend RESETS them to the defaults instead of keeping the user's), src/store/keybindings.ts:205-215 (unknown action ids accepted)
notes: FR-037/038 'carry your preferences to another machine' is met for 3 fields, and the one 'research engine' field it carries is invisible - the user's actual research setup (tier, per-stop models, SearXNG URL) and provider defaults silently do not travel. The import success message is unconditional, so a wrong file is reported as applied. Smallest fix: include useSearchSettingsStore {researchTier, researchModels, searxngUrl}, default provider/model and enabledModules in SettingsExport (version 2); in handleImportFile set 'ok' only when at least one recognised section was applied, else an error naming the expected shape; fix the copy to list what is actually exported.

title: Marketplace saves any NewsAPI key as 'configured' without a probe, and a rejected key is swallowed server-side: the feed silently stays RSS-only (and ~0.7 s slower per load) while the user believes NewsAPI breadth is on
repro: Marketplace -> Market News -> Configure -> NewsAPI key 'R15CANARY-newsapi-fake' -> Save credentials: keychain account plugin-secret:vysted-news:newsapi_key written, POST /plugins/vysted-news/config granted_secret_ids=[...], stateFor.configured=true - no request to NewsAPI (20-plugins-marketplace-replay.json configure:vysted-news). GET /news?limit=20 with X-Vysted-Newsapi-Key=<fake> -> 200, 20 items, sources = mint 5 / Economic Times 14 / Zerodha Pulse 1 (identical to the keyless call), 1.60 s vs 0.94 s keyless (F01/F02); the only trace is a sidecar log line 'news: NewsAPI source failed after retries: 401 Unauthorized'.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/20-plugins-marketplace-replay.json (P3 ops configure:vysted-news), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/http-log.jsonl F01-news-nokey / F02-news-fakekey, src/store/marketplace.ts:70-82 (configured = key present), :210-247 (configure writes secrets, no validation), sidecar/services/news_provider.py:316-329 (retry then return [] with a log warning), sidecar/routers/news.py:82-131 (bare list, no source-status field)
notes: Silent degrade of a paid-for BYOK source: the response shape (list[NewsItem]) has no place to say 'NewsAPI rejected your key', so the panel cannot tell the user; every load also pays the retry backoff. Smallest fix: probe NewsAPI once on Configure (GET /v2/top-headlines?pageSize=1 with the key; 401 -> reject with a message) and add a response header or wrapper field (e.g. X-Vysted-News-Sources: rss=ok,newsapi=unauthorized) that the News panel badges.

title: Settings > Modules 'AI Assistant' switch is a dead control: the chat module declares 0 panels and 0 commands and nothing reads its enabled flag
repro: Settings -> Advanced -> Modules: the row reads 'AI Assistant  0 panels · 0 commands' with a live switch (11-modules-region-replay.json moduleRows/moduleSectionText). Flip it off -> enabled['chat']=false, and the chat sidebar, composer and agents are unaffected, because nothing consumes that flag.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/11-modules-region-replay.json, src/modules/chat/index.ts:16-22 (panels: [], commands: []), `grep -rn 'enabled\["chat"\]\|enabled.chat' src` -> 0 hits, src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1720-1745 (every module gets a switch)
notes: A switch that does nothing teaches the user the Modules list is untrustworthy; 'AI Assistant' is the one module a privacy-minded user would try to turn off. Smallest fix: omit modules with no panels/commands from the list (or render them as 'always on' like Platform), or make the flag hide the agent column if disabling the assistant is a real product intent.

title: Saving a layout under a Hindi/Unicode or punctuated name fails as 'Could not save workspace "…" (HTTP 400)' - the sidecar's reason is discarded; a name over ~210 chars 500s (Errno 63 on the temp file)
repro: POST /workspace {name:'मेरा लेआउट'} -> 400 'Invalid workspace name ...: use letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, or underscores.' (D06); same for 'a/b', '../evil' (D04/D05). saveWorkspace() throws WorkspaceError('Could not save workspace "मेरा लेआउट" (HTTP 400).') so Settings -> Layouts shows only the status code. Names of 230-300 chars -> 500 Internal Server Error, sidecar log 'OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long: .../<name>.vysted-workspace.<pid>.<id>.tmp' (D07, D07b 230/236/240/250); the input has no maxLength and the 500 carries no CORS header, so the webview surfaces a generic failure.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/http-log.jsonl D04-D08, D07b-*, src/lib/workspace.ts:408-410 (status-only message), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1614-1624,1646-1652 (generic 'Layout operation failed.' fallback, no maxLength), sidecar/services/workspace_store.py:42-50 (regex rejects non-ASCII)
notes: For an India-first product, a Devanagari layout name is a normal input; the user gets a number instead of the rule. Smallest fix: surface extractSidecarDetail(body) in saveWorkspace's error, cap the name length in _validate_name (e.g. 120) so it 400s with a reason instead of 500ing, and either allow Unicode letters (\w with re.UNICODE, filename-safe) or say so under the input.

title: Disabling a module in Settings does not stop its panel from opening: openPanel resolves against every registered module, so the agent and host actions reopen a 'disabled' Portfolio or Notes
repro: Settings -> Advanced -> Modules: switch Portfolio off (enabled.portfolio=false; the hint says 'Disabled modules contribute no panels or ⌘K commands'). Then useWorkspaceStore.openPanel('portfolio') -> dockview addPanel({id:'portfolio', component:'portfolio-panel'}) is still called, and PanelHost's component map is built from ALL modules, so the panel renders. Every host action that opens a panel on apply does this: portfolio_add_position/update/delete -> openPanel('portfolio') (host-actions.ts:1349,1373,1387), write_note -> openPanel('notes') (:1191), agent open_panel. Control: openPanel('marketplace') adds the panel and openPanel('marketplace-panel') adds nothing (the dead CTA id, COD-frontend-panels-shell-chrome-2).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/13-openpanel-ids-disabled-module.json ('open:portfolio(disabled)' -> ['portfolio|portfolio-panel'], portfolioComponentMounted in enabled-only map = false), docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/settings-plugins/10-settings-plugins-replay.json S4-modules (after.findPanel = true while portfolioEnabled = false); src/store/modules.ts:83 (findPanel over get().modules, not enabledModules()), src/store/workspace.ts:92-100, src/components/PanelHost.tsx:123-126 (components from all modules), src/lib/host-actions.ts:935-940 (comment assumes a disabled module is a findPanel miss)
notes: The toggle hides a module from the ⌘K palette and panel menu only. The agent and the apply paths bring it straight back, so 'disabled' means 'not listed', and the host-actions comment shows the author believed a disabled module could not be opened. Smallest fix: have openPanel refuse (and return false) when the spec's module is disabled, by resolving through enabledModules(), and let open_panel's apply report that honestly ('Portfolio is disabled in Settings > Modules').
